jurisdiction.name: El Salvador
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: El Salvador regulates AI through the 2025 Law to Promote Artificial Intelligence and Technologies, which created the National AI Agency (ANIA), and ANIA's binding 2025 implementing rules requiring registration and impact assessments for high-stakes AI systems. A 2025 robotics law expressly covers robots that use AI, with ANIA as the competent authority, and ANIA published a National AI Strategy in 2026. The 2024 personal data protection law provides the data protection baseline.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the Official Journal and the national AI agency's website. Not yet verified from the official text: pending bills before the Legislative Assembly and any AI security rules from the cybersecurity agency. The AI risk-assessment framework and robotics rules the laws call for have not been published and are tracked as leads.

instruments.current_status: Decreto Legislativo N.° 234 of 26 February 2025, published in Diario Oficial No. 43, Tomo 446, 3 March 2025; in force eight days after publication (art. 29), i.e. 11 March 2025. Amended by Decreto Legislativo No. 363 of 16 July 2025 (Diario Oficial No. 134, Tomo 448, 18 July 2025), which recast ANIA as a decentralised body attached to the Presidency and added its budget and assets regime (art. 8-A), and implemented by ANIA Resolution 0001/2025.
instruments.summary: El Salvador's framework AI law, applying to anyone who develops, researches or applies AI, machine learning, generative models or similar technologies, or processes data for those activities. It creates the National Artificial Intelligence Agency (ANIA) and a National AI Development, Innovation and Application Register; registered actors gain safeguards such as no liability for research or sandbox testing and for third-party misuse, and protection of open-domain data use and open-source AI. It sets ethical principles (art. 5), requires ANIA to set a risk-assessment framework mandatory for systems handling confidential or personal data (art. 17), and obliges anyone using AI commercially or for access to rights or services to tell users when a decision was taken or driven by AI, explain it and allow challenge before a human (art. 18).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary AI statute: creates the national AI authority and register, AI-decision transparency and human-review rights, and liability safe harbours.

instruments.summary: ANIA's implementing rules for the AI law, with jurisdiction based on establishment, infrastructure or effects in El Salvador. They make registration with ANIA mandatory for operators of AI systems taking consequential decisions in health, credit and insurance, real-time biometric identification in public spaces, public powers and access to government services, employment and education, who must apply proportionate security measures, incident procedures and algorithmic impact assessments including bias testing; registration for the law's safeguards stays voluntary for others. They set an innovation sandbox, a presumption of conformity for certification to standards such as ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894 and the NIST AI RMF, rights to notification and human review of adverse automated decisions, voluntary measures for generative AI content, and a 12-month grace period for existing systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding implementing regulation of the AI law: mandatory registration and impact assessment for high-stakes AI, standards-based conformity and user rights.

instruments.summary: Sets the regulatory and incentive framework for researching, developing, manufacturing and deploying robotic technologies, expressly including 'robotic technology with applied artificial intelligence' that perceives its environment and takes decisions autonomously. It covers robots operating in publicly accessible spaces, interacting with people commercially, transporting people or goods on public roads and caring for minors, older people or persons with disabilities, with exceptions (e.g. drones, academic prototypes, building automation). ANIA is the competent authority through a Robotics Division and must set a risk-classification framework and technical safety rules and keep a catalogue of recognised standards (ISO/TS 15066, ISO 10218, ISO 13482, IEC 61508); principles include human primacy and control and proportionality.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding law on AI-enabled robots and autonomous systems, supervised by the national AI agency.

The AI law (art. 22) requires personal data in AI development and use to comply with this law.
instruments.summary: El Salvador's general data protection law, applying to public and private bodies processing personal data by manual, partly or fully automated means. It sets processing principles and ARCO-POL rights, including the right to object to profiling for commercial or direct-marketing purposes, and breach-notification duties. Supervision and sanctions sit with the State Cybersecurity Agency (ACE); it contains no AI-specific article but governs personal data used to train and run AI, as art. 22 of the AI law confirms.

instruments.current_status: Published by ANIA and linked from its home page as 'Estrategia Nacional de IA 2026'; the document is issued in English only (no Spanish version found). Only the year 2026 is printed; no day or month of publication is stated. It is El Salvador's first national AI strategy found.
instruments.summary: ANIA's national AI strategy, framed around 'velocity, sovereignty, deployment' and a pro-innovation stance that rejects precautionary regulation. It sets a target for AI to contribute about 20% of GDP by 2031 through sovereign compute and data centres, AI in government, education (Grok AI Tutor) and health (DoctorSV), talent and investment incentives and geothermal and nuclear energy for AI. It restates the legal framework (the AI law, its implementing rules and the Robot Law) with ANIA as single regulator, risk-calibrated obligations, mandatory registration for defined high-risk sectors, rights to know and challenge AI decisions and annual transparency reports.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national AI strategy; sets direction for AI adoption, infrastructure and the regulatory approach.
